rules.title: Provide compliant insulation and independent continuity for grounded conductors
rules.intent: Ensure the grounded (neutral) conductor is insulated equivalently to ungrounded conductors and remains continuous without relying on metallic enclosures, so the return path is never interrupted by hardware changes.
evidence_required: Conductor schedule or panel schedule showing grounded conductor insulation type and voltage rating
One-line diagram identifying system grounding (solidly grounded vs. impedance grounded) and system voltage
Wiring details showing grounded conductor spliced/terminated independent of enclosures, raceways, or cable armor

rules.title: Identify grounded-conductor terminals on devices, receptacles, plugs, and screw shells
rules.intent: Prevent reversed polarity by making the terminal intended for the grounded conductor visually identifiable on wiring devices.
evidence_required: Device and receptacle cut sheets showing white/silver grounded-terminal identification or 'W' marking
Fixture/lampholder details showing screw shell wired to the grounded conductor
Appliance listing documentation identifying the grounded circuit conductor terminal

rules.title: Install multiwire branch circuits with common origin, simultaneous disconnect, line-to-neutral loads, and grouping
rules.intent: Prevent shock and open-neutral overvoltage hazards on shared-neutral circuits by ensuring all ungrounded conductors disconnect together and conductors are identifiable.
evidence_required: Panel schedules showing multiwire circuits with common panelboard origin
Breaker layout showing multipole breakers or identified handle ties on multiwire circuits
Circuit directory/load list confirming line-to-neutral loads only
Wiring detail or note requiring grouping of multiwire circuit conductors in enclosures

rules.title: Provide ground-fault protection of equipment on large feeder disconnects
rules.intent: Protect equipment from destructive arcing ground faults on high-capacity solidly grounded wye feeders.
evidence_required: One-line diagram showing feeder disconnect ampere ratings and system grounding configuration
GFPE device specifications and settings for each feeder disconnect rated 1000 A or more
Voltage system documentation (e.g., 480Y/277 V) confirming applicability

rules.title: Size essential electrical system feeders per 215.2 and Article 220 Part III
rules.intent: Ensure essential electrical system feeders in health care facilities have ampacity for the maximum actual demand.
evidence_required: Feeder load calculations per Article 220 Part III
Feeder schedule showing conductor sizes and ampacities
Essential electrical system demand calculation and connected load summary

rules.title: Add a downstream level of ground-fault protection in health care facilities where service/feeder GFPE is provided
rules.intent: Localize ground-fault trips so a fault does not black out an entire health care facility serving critical care patients.
evidence_required: One-line diagram showing GFPE at service/feeder disconnect and at each next-level downstream feeder disconnect
GFPE relay/CT specifications for the downstream level
Riser diagram showing GFPE devices located upstream of essential electrical system transfer switches

rules.title: Scope: 240.15(B) governs use of single-pole circuit breakers as multiwire disconnecting means
rules.intent: Flag that the permissibility of single-pole breakers (with identified handle ties) as the simultaneous disconnecting means for multiwire branch circuits is governed by 240.15(B).
evidence_required: Panelboard breaker schedule identifying handle ties or multipole breakers on multiwire circuits
Manufacturer documentation for identified handle ties

rules.title: Bond electrode-type boiler metal parts per 250.102 with full-ampacity bonding jumper
rules.intent: Ensure exposed metal of high-voltage electrode boilers is bonded so fault/neutral current has a path at least as robust as the neutral conductor.
evidence_required: Boiler installation drawings showing bonding jumpers to pressure vessel/neutral
Bonding jumper size calculation compared to neutral conductor ampacity
Grounded neutral conductor specification (insulated 1000 V minimum, run with ungrounded conductors)

rules.title: Use flexible metal raceways as equipment grounding conductors only per 250.118 conditions
rules.intent: Limit reliance on FMC/LFMC/FMT as the fault-current path to the length, size, and fitting conditions of 250.118.
evidence_required: Wiring method schedule identifying where FMC/LFMC/FMT is used as the EGC
Circuit data (overcurrent device rating, raceway trade size, total length) demonstrating 250.118(5)/(6)/(7) conditions
Detail showing wire-type EGC where flexibility is required after installation

rules.title: Verify patient care space wiring methods qualify as equipment grounding conductors per 250.118
rules.intent: Guarantee the metallic raceway/cable armor serving patient care spaces is itself a recognized effective ground-fault current path.
evidence_required: Wiring method specification for patient care branch circuits (e.g., EMT, IMC, RMC, listed MC-HCF/AC with qualifying armor)
Cable listing documentation showing armor/sheath qualifies as an EGC per 250.118
Floor plans identifying patient care spaces served

rules.title: Size equipment grounding conductors and bonding jumpers per 250.122
rules.intent: Ensure EGCs and bonding jumpers in patient care wiring can carry fault current long enough for the overcurrent device to clear.
evidence_required: Circuit schedule listing overcurrent device rating and corresponding EGC size per Table 250.122
Feeder bonding jumper sizes on one-line diagram
Specification requiring insulated copper EGCs in patient care spaces

rules.title: Scope: 250.126 governs identification of wiring device equipment grounding conductor terminals
rules.intent: Flag that grounding-terminal identification on wiring devices (green/hexagonal terminal) is governed by 250.126, complementing grounded-terminal identification in 200.10.
evidence_required: Device cut sheets showing green-identified equipment grounding terminals
Receptacle specification referencing 250.126 terminal identification

rules.title: Install required equipment grounding conductors in accordance with 250.134
rules.intent: Keep the equipment grounding conductor with the circuit conductors so the fault-return path has low impedance, permitting separate runs only where 250.134 exceptions allow.
evidence_required: Conduit fill/circuit schedules showing EGC routed with circuit conductors
Grounding notes invoking 250.134 for flexible and nonmetallic raceway systems
Justification for any separately run EGC citing the applicable 250.134 exception

rules.title: Use the grounded circuit conductor to ground equipment only where 250.142 permits
rules.intent: Prevent objectionable neutral current on equipment enclosures by restricting neutral-as-ground connections to the limited supply-side cases 250.142 allows.
evidence_required: Grounding detail identifying any enclosure (busway, auxiliary gutter, service equipment) grounded via the grounded conductor
One-line diagram showing the connection is on the supply side of the service disconnecting means or otherwise within 250.142 permissions
Neutral-to-ground bonding location documentation

rules.title: Rate insulated grounded conductors of solidly grounded systems over 1000 V at not less than 600 V
rules.intent: Ensure the grounded neutral of medium-voltage solidly grounded systems has adequate insulation as described in 250.184(A).
evidence_required: Medium-voltage cable schedule showing neutral conductor insulation rating
One-line diagram identifying the solidly grounded neutral system over 1000 V

rules.title: Make equipment grounding conductor connections to busways and wireways per 250.8
rules.intent: Ensure EGC terminations at busway branches and wireway extensions use listed connection means that maintain the fault path.
evidence_required: Busway/wireway branch connection details showing listed lugs, pressure connectors, or machine-screw connections per 250.8
Notes requiring removal of nonconductive coatings at connection points per 250.12

rules.title: Scope: 300.13(B) governs device-independent continuity of multiwire grounded conductors
rules.intent: Flag that on multiwire branch circuits, the grounded conductor continuity must not depend on device connections, per 300.13(B).
evidence_required: Wiring detail showing pigtailed grounded conductors at devices on multiwire circuits
Specification note invoking 300.13(B) for multiwire branch circuits

rules.title: Ground and bond flexible metal conduit (FMC) installations
rules.intent: Ensure FMC used for vibration or movement carries a wire-type EGC, since flexing joints cannot be relied on as the fault path.
evidence_required: Equipment connection details (motors, transformers) showing wire-type EGC in FMC whips
Circuit schedule demonstrating 250.118(5) conditions where FMC serves as the EGC
Bonding jumper sizes per 250.102 where installed

rules.title: Ground and bond liquidtight flexible metal conduit (LFMC) installations
rules.intent: Ensure LFMC used for vibration or movement carries a wire-type EGC and relies on the conduit as EGC only within 250.118(6) limits.
evidence_required: Mechanical equipment connection details showing wire-type EGC in LFMC whips
Circuit schedule demonstrating 250.118(6) conditions where LFMC serves as the EGC
Hazardous-location grounding notes referencing 501.30/505.25 where applicable

rules.title: Install a separate equipment grounding conductor in PVC conduit
rules.intent: Provide a wire-type fault-current path because PVC conduit is nonmetallic and cannot serve as an equipment grounding conductor.
evidence_required: Conduit fill schedule showing EGC included in each PVC conduit run
EGC size per Table 250.122 on circuit schedules
Justification citing 250.134 or 250.142 for any run without an internal EGC

rules.title: Install a separate equipment grounding conductor in HDPE conduit
rules.intent: Provide a wire-type fault-current path because HDPE conduit is nonmetallic and cannot serve as an equipment grounding conductor.
evidence_required: Conduit fill schedule showing EGC included in each HDPE conduit run
EGC size per Table 250.122 on circuit schedules
Justification citing 250.134 or 250.142 for any run without an internal EGC

rules.title: Use RTRC and fittings constructed of suitable resistant nonmetallic material
rules.intent: Ensure reinforced thermosetting resin conduit withstands its environment (moisture, chemicals, impact, sunlight, burial loading).
evidence_required: RTRC product listing/labels (e.g., Type XW where exposed to damage)
Marking documentation per 355.120 (material type, sunlight resistance)
Installation specification matching conduit type to aboveground/underground use

rules.title: Install a separate equipment grounding conductor in RTRC conduit
rules.intent: Provide a wire-type fault-current path because RTRC conduit is nonmetallic and cannot serve as an equipment grounding conductor.
evidence_required: Conduit fill schedule showing EGC included in each RTRC conduit run
EGC size per Table 250.122 on circuit schedules
Justification citing 250.134 or 250.142 for any run without an internal EGC

rules.title: Install a separate equipment grounding conductor in LFNC conduit
rules.intent: Provide a wire-type fault-current path because LFNC conduit is nonmetallic and cannot serve as an equipment grounding conductor.
evidence_required: Conduit fill schedule showing EGC included in each LFNC conduit run
EGC size per Table 250.122 on circuit schedules
Justification citing 250.134 or 250.142 for any run without an internal EGC

rules.title: Make branches from busways with permitted wiring methods and compliant grounding connections
rules.intent: Ensure busway branch circuits use recognized wiring methods and that separate EGCs are properly connected to the busway.
evidence_required: Busway layout showing branch tap devices and wiring methods
Bus drop cable listing and support/strain-relief details
EGC connection detail at busway per 250.8/250.12

rules.title: Make extensions from metal wireways with grounding-capable wiring methods
rules.intent: Preserve the equipment grounding path when circuits leave a metal wireway.
evidence_required: Wireway layout showing extension wiring methods
EGC termination detail at the wireway per 250.8/250.12

rules.title: Restrict RTRC in Class I, Division 2 locations to installations permitted by 501.10(B)(1)(6)
rules.intent: Prevent nonmetallic conduit from being used in classified locations except where the Class I, Division 2 wiring method rules specifically allow it.
evidence_required: Hazardous area classification drawings identifying Class I, Division 2 boundaries
Wiring method schedule for classified areas citing 501.10(B)(1)(6) permission
RTRC listing documentation for the classified-location use

rules.title: Comply with 501.30 grounding and bonding in Class I locations
rules.intent: Ensure bonding-type fittings and grounding continuity in classified areas so fault current cannot arc at loose raceway joints and ignite flammable atmospheres.
evidence_required: Hazardous area classification plan
Bonding details showing bonding-type fittings/jumpers through the classified area back to the supply grounding point
Wire-type EGC specification for flexible raceways within the classified area

rules.title: Ground and bond all metal wiring and equipment in commercial garages
rules.intent: Eliminate shock and ignition hazards in repair garages by grounding all metal wiring components and portable equipment regardless of voltage.
evidence_required: Garage area classification plan per 511.3
Grounding/bonding notes covering raceways, cable armor, and portable equipment
Receptacle schedule showing grounding-type devices for portable/pendant circuits

rules.title: Scope: apply Article 514 to motor fuel dispensing facilities
rules.intent: Trigger Article 514 classification, wiring, sealing, disconnect, and grounding rules wherever motor fuels are dispensed.
evidence_required: Site plan identifying dispensing devices, tanks, and vents
Hazardous area classification drawings per Table 514.3(B)(1)/(B)(2)
AHJ determination letter where unclassified status is claimed

rules.title: Ground and bond all metal wiring and equipment at motor fuel dispensing facilities
rules.intent: Prevent static/fault ignition sources at fuel dispensers by grounding and bonding all metal parts regardless of voltage.
evidence_required: Grounding and bonding plan for dispenser islands and canopy circuits
Threaded metal conduit and bonding fitting details within classified areas
EGC continuity documentation for underground nonmetallic conduit runs

rules.title: Ground and bond all metal wiring and equipment in spray/dipping/coating process areas
rules.intent: Remove ignition sources in finishing process areas by grounding and bonding all metal parts per the applicable classified-location rules.
evidence_required: Process area classification plan per 516.4/516.5
Grounding/bonding details for booths, ducts, conveyors, and containers
Static grounding provisions for conductive objects in the spray area

rules.title: Provide redundant equipment grounding for patient care space wiring
rules.intent: Ensure two independent ground-fault current paths (metallic wiring method plus insulated copper EGC) protect patients from potential differences.
evidence_required: Floor plans designating patient care space categories
Branch circuit wiring method specification showing both metallic raceway/armor and insulated copper EGC
Typical receptacle grounding detail for patient care spaces

rules.title: Install patient care branch circuits in metal raceway or metallic-armored cable qualifying as an EGC
rules.intent: Provide the first (mechanical) ground-fault current path for patient care branch circuits.
evidence_required: Wiring method schedule for patient care branch circuits
Cable listing (e.g., Type MC-HCF/AC) showing armor qualifies as an EGC
Raceway specifications (EMT/IMC/RMC) for patient care areas

rules.title: Connect patient care receptacles, boxes, and fixed equipment to an insulated green copper EGC
rules.intent: Provide the second (wire-type) redundant grounding path in patient care spaces.
evidence_required: Typical patient care receptacle wiring detail showing insulated green copper EGC
Specification requiring green insulation along the EGC's entire length
EGC sizing per 250.122 on circuit schedules

rules.title: Keep the required patient-care EGC connected to boxes/enclosures, not to isolated ground receptacle terminals
rules.intent: Preserve the redundant grounding of boxes and fixed equipment when isolated ground receptacles are used outside the patient care vicinity.
evidence_required: Isolated ground receptacle wiring detail showing two EGCs (green and green/yellow-stripe)
Receptacle schedule confirming no isolated ground receptacles within patient care vicinities
Conductor identification specification for IG circuits

rules.title: Design and install isolated power systems with per-conductor disconnection, isolation, and identification
rules.intent: Limit first-fault current in critical and wet/anesthetizing spaces by keeping the secondary ungrounded, protected, and identifiable.
evidence_required: Isolated power panel listing documentation (listed isolated power equipment)
Single-line diagram of the isolated power system showing transformer, LIM, and per-conductor OCP
Conductor identification schedule (orange/brown/yellow with stripes)
Room assignments showing one isolation transformer per operating room

rules.title: Make health care ground-fault protection fully selective and performance test each level
rules.intent: Guarantee that a downstream ground fault opens only the feeder device, keeping the rest of the critical-care facility energized.
evidence_required: GFPE selectivity coordination study with time-current curves
Manufacturer setting recommendations and applied settings
Field performance test report for each GFPE level, signed and dated

rules.title: Wire Category 2 (general care) patient bed locations with dual-source circuits and eight hospital-grade receptacles
rules.intent: Provide power redundancy and grounded, durable receptacles at general care patient beds.
evidence_required: Patient room power plans showing critical branch and normal system circuits per bed
Panel schedules confirming common normal-system panelboard and no multiwire circuits
Receptacle count per bed location and hospital-grade listing
Receptacle/coverplate color-coding and circuit identification schedule

rules.title: Wire Category 1 (critical care) bed locations with dedicated critical-branch circuits, 14 receptacles, and reference-point grounding
rules.intent: Maximize power availability and grounding integrity where equipment failure is likely to cause major injury or death.
evidence_required: Critical care room power plans with per-bed circuit and receptacle counts
Operating room receptacle schedule (36 minimum, source split documented)
Grounding detail showing insulated copper EGC to the reference grounding point
Feeder raceway bonding details (grounding bushings/jumpers per 250.122)

rules.title: Provide special shock protection in wet procedure locations
rules.intent: Protect patients and staff in wet procedure areas by limiting first-fault ground current or interrupting power at GFCI thresholds.
evidence_required: Wet procedure location risk assessment/designation by the governing body
Isolated power system design or GFCI protection schedule for the space
Listing documentation for isolated power equipment where used

rules.title: Apply Article 700 to the essential electrical system branches except as amended by Article 517
rules.intent: Anchor the essential electrical system to emergency-system installation rules while recognizing the health care amendments.
evidence_required: Essential electrical system design narrative citing Article 700 compliance with 517.26 modifications
Emergency lighting circuiting showing supply from a 700.12-compliant source
Transfer switch and branch separation documentation

rules.title: Serve Category 1 (critical care) spaces from a Type 1 essential electrical system
rules.intent: Ensure the highest-reliability three-branch EES backs up spaces where power failure is likely to cause major injury or death.
evidence_required: EES classification statement (Type 1) on drawings
Space category designations by the facility governing body
Single-line diagram of the three-branch Type 1 EES

rules.title: Provide two independent power sources with protected locations and separated feeders for the EES
rules.intent: Guarantee an alternate source and physically separated distribution so one event cannot interrupt both normal and alternate power.
evidence_required: One-line diagram showing normal and alternate sources
Generator/fuel-cell/battery specifications with 10-second start capability and on-site fuel storage
Site plan showing physical separation of normal and alternate feeders
Flood/seismic siting documentation for EES components

rules.title: Configure the Type 1 EES with three branches, independent protected wiring, adequate capacity, and coordinated OCPDs
rules.intent: Keep life safety and critical power available and isolated from failures in other wiring during loss of normal power.
evidence_required: EES single-line diagram showing life safety, critical, and equipment branches with transfer switches
Wiring method specification for life safety/critical branch raceways
EES identification/marking plan (25 ft interval labeling)
Selective coordination study for OCPDs beyond 0.1 second
Demand calculation for EES capacity and feeder sizing

rules.title: Apply Type 2 EES requirements to nursing home and limited care Category 2 spaces
rules.intent: Scope the Type 2 essential electrical system rules to general care spaces in nursing homes, limited care facilities, and CA correctional/psychiatric facilities.
evidence_required: Facility licensing/occupancy documentation (nursing home, limited care)
EES classification (Type 2) and coverage plan
Admitting/discharge policy where the freestanding exception is claimed
Battery system capacity calculation (1.5 hours) for the exception

rules.title: Divide the Type 2 EES into life safety and equipment branches kept independent of other wiring
rules.intent: Preserve life-safety power integrity in nursing homes and limited care facilities by branch separation and identification.
evidence_required: Type 2 EES single-line diagram with life safety and equipment branches
Transfer switch schedule with continuous load calculations
Raceway separation notes and identification/color-coding scheme

rules.title: Restore Type 2 EES life safety and equipment branch functions automatically within 10 seconds
rules.intent: Ensure egress lighting, alarms, and essential equipment return quickly after normal power loss, and keep the life safety branch limited to listed functions.
evidence_required: Transfer switch timing documentation (10-second restoration)
Life safety branch load schedule limited to 517.43(A)-(G) functions
Generator start and load-acceptance test report

rules.title: Connect the equipment branch for delayed automatic restoration at time-lag intervals
rules.intent: Stage equipment loads onto the alternate source after life safety loads to avoid overloading the generator.
evidence_required: Load-shed/step-load sequence documentation for the equipment branch
Equipment branch load schedule mapped to 517.44(A)/(B) categories
Generator sizing calculation supporting staged connection

rules.title: Install anesthetizing-location wiring and equipment per hazardous, above-hazardous, and unclassified rules
rules.intent: Prevent ignition of flammable anesthetics and maintain grounding integrity for wiring within, above, and outside classified anesthetizing locations.
evidence_required: Anesthetizing location classification determination (flammable vs. nonflammable agents)
Isolated power system design for flammable anesthetizing locations
Wiring method schedule for within/above/unclassified zones
Hospital-grade and Class I Group C receptacle listings

rules.title: Ground all metal raceways and fixed equipment in anesthetizing areas
rules.intent: Equalize potential on all conductive surfaces around anesthetized patients and satisfy Class I grounding where flammable agents are used.
evidence_required: Grounding plan for anesthetizing areas
EGC termination details for fixed equipment and raceways
Equipment voltage documentation for any low-voltage exception claims

rules.title: Prevent hazardous grounding interconnection in signal transmission between patient appliances
rules.intent: Stop ground loops through patient-connected appliances located in different grounding environments.
evidence_required: Signal/data cabling riser showing isolation devices between patient location and remote appliances
Reference grounding point documentation for interconnected patient care vicinity appliances

rules.title: Use hazardous-location-approved traveling cables in classified locations
rules.intent: Ensure elevator traveling cables in classified locations are of types the hazardous-location articles permit.
evidence_required: Hazardous area classification drawings for the hoistway/garage
Traveling cable listing documentation for the applicable class/division or zone
Elevator wiring specification citing the permitting hazardous-location section

rules.title: Supply health care emergency lighting and on-premises alternate sources per 700.12
rules.intent: Ensure emergency lighting in health care facilities transfers to a code-compliant emergency source and that on-premises sources meet stored-energy requirements.
evidence_required: Emergency lighting circuit schedule showing transfer to the alternate source
Generator fuel storage or battery capacity calculations per 700.12
Transfer switch documentation for emergency lighting circuits
